decisions.reason: The formal family-of-measurable-sections definition is sound, but the final real-valued gloss incorrectly identifies a pivot with a statistic. In the discrete location experiment, q_theta(x)=x-theta has common masses 1/3 at -1, 0, 1 under P_theta, yet depends on theta and is not one parameter-independent data map. This is a nonfatal terminology defect: the formal definition and inversion arguments already use parameter-indexed sections. Replaced only the gloss to allow parameter dependence explicitly; no claim was weakened.

The repaired gloss agrees with that definition and preserves noninvertibility and noninterval caveats. The boundary contract remains accurate and passed strict checking; the owning manifest now mirrors the complete Definition. This is my repair review, not independent acceptance.

exact_interface_change.before:
For $S=\mathbb R$, a pivot is a real-valued statistic whose sampling
distribution is parameter-free.
exact_interface_change.after:
For $S=\mathbb R$, a pivot is a parameter-indexed family of measurable
real-valued quantities with a common sampling law. The maps $q_\theta$
may depend on the unknown parameter.
